title: Sourdough day 3: bubbles appearing. The culture is alive.
context: There's something deeply satisfying about nurturing a living thing that has its own schedule. I check on it like a parent.

title: Sourdough Scoring Patterns — Bread Art
context: Decorative scoring techniques for artisan loaves. Ear development. The blade work is meditative.

title: The Microbiome of Sourdough
context: Each starter develops a unique microbiome based on location, flour, environment. My starter is literally unique to my kitchen.

title: First bake attempt. Overproofed. Flat as a frisbee. But the smell — incredible.
context: Failed technically, succeeded emotionally. The house smelled like a bakery for hours.

title: Troubleshooting Sourdough: Common Mistakes
context: Underproofed vs overproofed, hydration issues, oven spring problems. Every failure teaches something.

title: Mycelium as the new name for Rhizome
context: The project evolves: from Rhizome to Mycelium. The ecology metaphor deepens. Mycelium is the underground network that feeds the whole forest.

title: How Notion Thinks About Data Models
context: Blocks, databases, relations. The primitives of personal software. Interesting but still tool-first, not person-first.

title: Unbody — AI-native content platform
context: The company behind Mycelium. Headless CMS with AI understanding. The infrastructure layer that makes Mycelium possible.

title: Thread detection as the core feature
context: The system should discover threads of attention organically, not through user-created tags. The user saves, the system understands.

title: The thread registry idea: a learner that just watches everything and maintains a list of active threads
context: Like a table of contents for attention. Always updating. Shows you what you're paying attention to even when you don't realize it.

title: What if Mycelium could tell you when you're about to burn out?
context: Combining attention tracking with energy patterns. If save velocity spikes, that's a warning sign. The tool becomes a mirror.

title: Mycelium is not a productivity tool. It's a self-awareness tool. That's the key distinction.
